title: Descent of t-exact coefficient families and canonical comparison maps
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its directed set of finite subextensions $E$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For each $E$ let $R_E=\mathcal O_E$ with uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}},\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ be $R_E$-linear triangulated categories [def-weil-linear-category, def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Suppose their raw scalar localizations $\mathcal C_E=\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}[1/\pi_E]$ and $\mathcal D_E=\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}[1/\pi_E]$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] have distinguished triangles isomorphic to localized integral triangles, and bounded t-structures whose halves are the isomorphism closures of the images of the corresponding integral halves. Suppose exact t-exact coefficient transition functors $T^{\mathcal C}_{L/E},T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}$ between rational stages are supplied, with identity and associative tower comparisons. Suppose the corresponding pair categories are triangulated: their objects are $(E,K)$, their morphisms are the directed colimits of morphisms after extension to common finite fields, and their distinguished triangles are those isomorphic to triangles from one finite stage. Suppose the isomorphism closures of finite-stage halves give bounded t-structures there, with truncations and their canonical maps computed at a finite stage.

Let $F_E^{\mathrm{int}}:\mathcal C_E^{\mathrm{int}}\to\mathcal D_E^{\mathrm{int}}$ be $R_E$-linear exact functors with specified linear shift comparisons. Assume each preserves the two integral halves. Let $F_E$ be their additive extensions on fractions, and suppose natural isomorphisms $\beta_{L/E}:T^{\mathcal D}_{L/E}F_E\cong F_LT^{\mathcal C}_{L/E}$ are supplied as isomorphisms of exact functors, compatible with their shift comparisons, equal to the identity for $L=E$ and compatible with the tower associators. They define the functor $F_\Omega(E,K)=(E,F_EK)$, acting on a common-stage arrow $u$ by $\beta_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}F_L(u)\beta_{\mathrm{source}}$.

Then every $F_E$ and $F_\Omega$ is exact and t-exact and restricts to an exact functor of hearts. For each of these functors $F$, every integer $m$, and either sign, there are unique natural isomorphisms
$$\alpha^-_{F,m}:F\tau^{\le m}\cong\tau^{\le m}F,\qquad\alpha^+_{F,m}:F\tau^{\ge m}\cong\tau^{\ge m}F$$
with $\iota_{FK}^m\alpha^-_{F,m,K}=F(\iota_K^m)$ and $\alpha^+_{F,m,K}F(\pi_K^m)=\pi_{FK}^m$, where $\iota^m:\tau^{\le m}\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\pi^m:\mathrm{id}\to\tau^{\ge m}$ are the canonical maps. Composing these and the shift comparison gives $F\mathcal H^j\cong\mathcal H^jF$, where $\mathcal H^j=(\tau^{\ge j}\tau^{\le j})[j]$. The $\alpha$ and cohomology comparisons commute with every $\beta_{L/E}$ and with successive coefficient extensions. At $\Omega$ they are represented by the finite-stage comparisons, independently of further enlargement of the stage.

proof.text: The fraction extension is already supplied, with a shift-compatible factorization Q_C ⋙ F_E ≅ F_E_int ⋙ Q_D. The stipulated triangle description makes Q_D triangulated. Transport exactness of F_E_int ⋙ Q_D across that factorization, then represent each rational distinguished triangle as a Q_C-image and apply Functor.mapTriangleCompIso. This proves exactness of the specified F_E directly; no construction or uniqueness of a semilinear extension is required.

proof.text: Represent a rational object in either half at zero by a localized integral object. Apply F_E to the representing isomorphism, followed by the supplied localization factorization. Integral half preservation and the target half description prove preservation at zero. Use the specified comparison for shift by every integer to transfer this to all cutoffs.

proof.text: Use the existing StageSystem.Morphism.functor and descNatTrans. The stage shift comparisons form a compatible Hom of stage-system morphisms, by NatTrans.shift_app_comm for beta. Descend them to natural isomorphisms. Their zero and addition equations follow by applying the stage inclusion to the corresponding finite-stage equations, using functor_map_ι and the induced pair-category shift formulas. The inclusion comparison commutes with this shift. Represent a distinguished pair triangle at a stage, apply finite-stage exactness and the inclusion square of mapTriangle, and transport along its isomorphism. For both halves, use the assumed stage presentations. These also prove t-exactness of each inclusion.

proof.text: Construct the actual heart restriction by ObjectProperty.lift. T-exactness preserves the intersection of the two halves, and additivity follows from the faithful heart inclusion. Apply the short-exact/distinguished-triangle criterion before and after mapping its triangle by F; the third arrow is F(delta) followed by the specified shift comparison.

proof.text: For each finite functor, transition, inclusion and descended functor use eTruncLTIso and eTruncGEIso. Their counit/unit equations are the existing upstream equations; uniqueness is lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison. Take q to be truncationCohomologyComparison. Its proved formula is precisely q_formula after expanding truncLE and truncGELE. The square theorem supplies the beta and inclusion squares. For an isomorphism from a composite to a third functor, combine the comparison composition equations with transformation naturality, for both truncations and q. Apply this to the tower associators and transIso.

proof.text: The inclusion comparisons are uniquely normalized, so any supplied finite-stage truncation computation respecting the canonical maps equals them. The inclusion square therefore gives the finite-stage representation, and the transIso composite square gives independence of further enlargement, including cohomology. The theorem already records these as SquareCompatible and CompositeCompatible equations.
